captions.text: Open Calls and choose the community care check-in exercise.
Confirm its training title and department call number before you continue.
The left panel identifies Engine 51, the apparatus selected in Unit.
No Active Call means that opening a call to read it has not itself assigned
that call as the unit's response.
This example uses a fictional community paramedicine and
mental health outreach visit.
The same check-in tools can support other department workflows.
In Call Details, open Check-In.
The Personnel card shows the check-in type, the time since the
last entry, and its current state.
Here the last check-in was ten minutes ago, the counter reads ten of
sixty minutes, and the state is OK.
These values help a coordinator see when a scheduled update is due.
The sixty-minute interval comes from department configuration; it is not a
duration that the crew sets on this card.
Open History below the timer.
The saved Personnel entry includes its timestamp and note, so you can
distinguish an earlier check-in from an update you are about to enter.
In this exercise the note identifies a scheduled software check-in
for the community care visit.
Check the history before repeating an update, especially when a crew
changes or another team member may already have checked in.
A saved software entry does not establish someone's physical location.

scenes.title: Add a note and confirm the check-in

captions.text: Select Check In on the Personnel card.
In the form, confirm Personnel under Select check-in type, then
use Add note to explain the update.
Our note says this is a follow-up software check-in after reviewing history.
Review the wording and select Confirm Check-In.
Use a short, useful note that follows your department's procedures.
For search and rescue or security patrols, describe the agreed
reporting update without adding unnecessary personal details.
After confirmation, review the Personnel card again.
The displayed age is now zero minutes, the counter reads zero of sixty
minutes, and the state remains OK.
This is the observed reset for this check-in.
A timer reset and a unit status change are separate operations.
Wildland contractors and industrial response teams can use the same
distinction when coordinating regular reports during a longer assignment.

scenes.title: Verify the new saved history entry

captions.text: Open History again and read the newest entry.
The follow-up note appears above the earlier scheduled
check-in, with its own timestamp.
This is how you verify that the note was stored, rather
than simply left in the form.
Check both the timer and history when learning this workflow.
Your department decides the reporting interval and escalation procedure;
the app supplies the check-in controls and a record of the updates.
